Hi Dana — thanks for the questions, happy to dig in. Short answers below and attached is a small CSV with the split numbers: caching_on vs caching_off and the quantization profile used.

- Caching: the benchmark Marissa shared had prefix/KV caching enabled for warm-start conditions. With caching OFF we saw p50 increase ~18% and throughput drop ~20% under the same batching config. The attached redwood-bench-2026.csv contains both series (columns: run,cache_enabled,p50_ms,p95_ms,throughput_rps).
- Quantization: we tested with an int8-aware profile (symmetric activation quantization + per-channel weight quantization). Quality delta was <1.5% on our internal eval set for typical completions; latency improvements were ~12% vs fp16 on the same hardware.

Operational notes: if ACME wants deterministic tail behavior, we recommend enabling a small KV cache (size tuned to your session reuse — we can estimate that if you share a sample prefix distribution). Also consider an async-batching window of 5ms to smooth throughput spikes without materially impacting p50.

I've attached the CSV export and a short snippet of the harness command we used so your infra team can reproduce locally. Happy to hop on a quick call with Tom if you'd like to walk through the numbers.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
